The Court made the following:
Judgment:
This M.A.C.M.A. is directed against the award, dated 15.11.2017 in M.V.OP.No.729 of 2013, on the
file of Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Guntur, Guntur
Distri
ct ("Tribunal" for short),

where under the Tribunal as against the claim of the claimant to award a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- as compensation, with regard to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 30.01.2013 at 01.15 p.m. near Madhina Hotel, Pedana Town and Mandal, Krishna District, allowed a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation.
2. The parties to this M.A.C.M.A. will hereinafter be referred to as described before the learned Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The claimant, being represented by his mother and natural guardian, laid a claim on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Guntur, Guntur District,
under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act and Rules 455 and 476 of A.P.M.V. Rules, seeking compensation with regard to injuries received by him in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The case of the petitioner, in brief, according to the averments in the motor vehicle accident claim, is that:
(i) The petitioner is the resident of Pedana and at present he is staying in old Guntur.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing No. AP 11 Z 82 (offending vehicle for short).

(ii) On 30.01.2013, the petitioner went to his school namely B.G.K. Z.P.H. School,
Pedana where he was studying 9th Class.

At about 01.00 p.m., while he was returning to his house for lunch on his bicycle, on the left side of the road margin and when he reached near Madina Hotel, the offending bus driven by respondent no.2 in a rash and negligent manner and without blowing horn dashed the bicycle of the petitioner on its back side and due to that the petitioner fell down and the front tire of the bus ran over the right hand of the petitioner, due to which the petitioner sustained crush injury to his right hand and other multiple injuries all over his body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Machilipatnam and thereafter, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Guntur for better treatment as his grand-parents reside in Guntur and he took treatment at Government Hospital, Guntur for a period of three months and he underwent surgery to his right hand and to right hand fingers.
(iii) A case in crime No.14 of 2013 for the offence under Section 337 I.P.C. was registered at Pedana Police Station against the respondent No.2.
(iv) The petitioner was aged about 14 years and he was hale and healthy and was studying 9th class by the date of accident.
Due to the accident, the petitioner is unable to pursue his studies, unable to write anything and unable to do his daily works.
The petitioner lost his bright future due to the accident.

Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-
to the petitioner.
5. The respondent No.2 did not contest the case and remained exparte before the Tribunal.
However, the Respondent No.1 who is the employer of the respondent No.2 got filed the counter denying the case of the petitioner and putting the petitioner to strict proof of the averments.

The contention of the respondent No.1 in substance is that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending bus and in-fact there was negligence on the part of the petitioner, as he was driving the bicycle in a negligent manner and that compensation claimed is excessive and arbitrary.

6. On the basis of the said pleadings, the Tribunal settled the following issues for trial:
(1) Whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle of A.P.S.R.T.C. Bus bearing No. AP 11 Z 82?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and against whom?

(3) To what relief?
7. During course of trial before the Tribunal, mother and natural guardian of the petitioner was examined as PW.1.
Claimant got further examined PW.2, the medical officer and got marked Ex.A1 to A.8.
No evidence was adduced by the respondent No.1.
Further, through the examination of PW.2, Ex.X1-case sheet was marked.

8. The learned Tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral and documentary evidence, answered the issues in favour of the petitioner-claimant and awarded a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit and that both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation within one month from the date of judgment and that on such deposit, the guardian of the petitioner is entitled to withdraw a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- and the rest of the amount shall be kept in any nationalized Bank until the petitioner attains majority.

9. Felt aggrieved that the compensation so awarded is excessive and further it is not in accordance with law, the unsuccessful respondent No.1 i.e., A.P.S.R.T.C. filed the present M.A.C.M.A.
10.

Now in deciding the present M.A.C.M.A., the points that arise for consideration are as follows:
(1) Whether the claimant before the Tribunal proved that he received injuries in a Motor Vehicle accident, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of respondent No.2 in the claim i.e., driver of the A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing No. AP 11 Z 82 ?

(2) Whether the award, dated 15.11.2017 in M.V.OP.No.729 of 2013, on the file of Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Guntur,
Guntur District, awarding compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- to the claimant is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to interfere with the same?

entities.text:
Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Guntur,
Guntur District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Point Nos.1 and 2:
11. PW.1 before the Tribunal was no other than the mother of the petitioner.
She put forth the facts in her chief examination affidavit in tune with the pleadings.
Through her examination, Exs. A1 to A8 are marked.
Ex . A1
is copy of F.I.R. in Crime No.14 of 2013 of Pedana Police Station.
Ex . A2
is copy of charge sheet.
Ex . A3
is copy of wound certificate.
Ex . A4
is discharge summary issued by Yashaswi Hospitals, Guntur
. Ex .
A5 is final bill issued by Yashaswi Hospitals, Guntur for an amount of Rs.1,04,950/-.
Ex.A6 is bunch of medical bills for a sum of Rs.23,775/-.

Ex.A7 is bunch of medical bills issued by Sri Balaji Physiotherapy and Sports Rehabilitation Clinic for an amount of Rs.24,700/- and Ex.A8 is cash receipts issued by Yashaswi Hospitals for an amount of Rs.2,400/-.

sentences.text:
Further, the petitioner examined PW.2, medical officer who treated the injured and the evidence of PW.2 in brief is that the petitioner was admitted in the Hospital on 31.01.2013, due to crush injury of right hand wrist and loss of thumb phalanges and that on the same date debridement,
external fixation and KY fixator were done and regular dressings were done.
On 22.02.2013 skin grafting of right hand was done and on 08.03.2013, he was discharged.
Ex.X1 is the case sheet.
Injury was grievous.
There is loss of right thumb and deformity of remaining four fingers with loss of right wrist function and the disability is 60%, which is permanent in nature.
Exs . A3
to Ex.A8
were issued by Yashaswi Hospitals, Guntur.

13. Sri Vinod Kumar Taralada, learned standing counsel for the appellant-A.P.S.R.T.C., would contend that the accident occurred was due to the rash and negligent act of the injured and that the Tribunal did not appreciate the evidence in proper perspective.

He would submit that mainly the grievance of appellant is that the Tribunal awarded compensation on the ground of disability,
though the disability was not proved.
He would submit that an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- is not at all warranted in the circumstances of the case, as such it is liable to be decreased.
14. Sri K.Rama Krishna Reddy, learned counsel for the respondent No.1, would canvass a contention that the Tribunal rightly considered the evidence adduced by the claimant.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not enter into the witness box and did not contest the claim.
Evidence on record reveals that the incident occurred was due to rash and negligent act of respondent No.2 in driving the offending vehicle.

Though the disability affecting earnings was not proved, but the fact remained is that claimant lost right thumb according to the evidence of PW.2 and as such there was deformity in the remaining four fingers of his right hand.
The Tribunal rightly awarded a lump-sum amount of Rs.1,50,000/-, on account of the said disability.
He would seek to support the judgment of the Tribunal on the ground that the Tribunal rightly appreciated the evidence and awarded the aforesaid sum.

15. Firstly, this Court would like to deal with as to whether the petitioner proved the rash and negligent act against respondent No.2, the driver of the offending vehicle, and that on account of it,
he received grievous injuries.
As seen from the evidence of PW.1, she was the defacto complainant.
It was basing on the statement of the injured himself, the F.I.R. was registered.
So, F.I.R. was registered basing on the statement of the injured and PW.1 supported the case of the claimant.
It is no doubt true that she was no other than the mother of the injured.
But her evidence was in accordance with the record.
As seen from Ex.A2, police completed the investigation by filing charge sheet alleging rash and negligent act against the respondent No.2.
For obvious reasons, respondent No.2 remained exparte.
He did not choose to contest the claim of the petitioner.
For obvious reasons, even the respondent No.1 did not step into the witness box.
So, what all the facts averred on behalf of the claimant in the form of examination of PW.1 and marking of Exs.A1 to Ex.A8 remained un-rebutted.
A perusal of Ex.A3-wound certificate of the petitioner goes to reveal that the petitioner received grievous injury.
There was crush injury of right hand wrist and loss of thumb phalanges.
The injuries received by the petitioner were not disputed.
So, the petitioner was able to prove that accident occurred was due to rash and negligent act of respondent No.2 and that he received grievous injury.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now, as respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the driver, petitioner is entitled to compensation from both the respondents.
17. Now coming to the quantum of compensation, the medical expenditure, which the petitioner claimed under Exs.A5, A6, A7 and A8, is not at all in dispute during the course of cross- examination.
So, the medical bills under Exs.A5 to Ex.A8 are construed to Rs.1,55,825/- and the Tribunal rounded of it as Rs.1,56,000/-.

Considering the evidence of PW.1 and the nature of injury,
the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.24,000/- for future medical expenses and follow up and the said amount cannot be said to be un-reasonable.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards special diet and attendant charges.
The injured was aged about 14 years at the time of accident.
He lost his right thumb.
So, the amount of Rs.20,000/- granted towards special diet and attendant charges, appears to be quietly reasonable.
Coming to other heads of compensation, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering and it cannot be said to be unreasonable.
18. Now, turning to another head of Rs.1,50,000/- granted towards the disability, admittedly, it is a case where PW.2 stated that petitioner sustained disability, which is 60%.
The Tribunal took into consideration the fact that the petitioner did not appear before the medical board which is competent to determine the disability.

However, Tribunal placed reliance on the evidence of PW.2,
because he is a qualified Orthopedic Surgeon to believe the case of the petitioner that he lost his right thumb and there is deformity to remaining four fingers of the right hand.
Absolutely, the loss of right thumb of the petitioner which was crucial for wrist function of the right hand was not in dispute.
It was also not in dispute that on account of loss of right thumb there would be certain form of inconvenience to the remaining fingers.
As evident from the judgment of the Tribunal, it is not a case where the Tribunal upheld the disability claimed by the petitioner.
The Tribunal took into consideration the overall deprivation of right thumb and consequential inconvenience.
The Tribunal allowed a lump-sum amount of Rs.1,50,000/- towards the disability.
So, it is not a case of disability affecting earnings and there was no dispute that there was the loss of right thumb and consequent inconvenience to the remaining fingers.
So, the Tribunal rightly awarded a lump- sum of Rs.1,50,000/- under this head.
19. Having regard to the above, absolutely this Court does not find any tenable grounds to interfere with the well reasoned order of the Tribunal.
20. In the result, the M.A.C.M.A. is dismissed, but under the circumstances without costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.14.02.2024.
